machine.affinity: both inherit the benchmark process CPU availability; no per-executable restriction

build-rust.sh.text:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
export RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native'
export CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$PWD/.build/rust-target"
cargo build --release --locked --manifest-path upstream/Cargo.toml
mkdir -p bin
cp "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release/ripwc" bin/ripwc-rust

upstream/Cargo.toml.text:
[package]
name = "ripwc"
version = "1.0.0"
edition = "2021"
authors = ["LuminousToaster", "https://github.com/LuminousToaster"]

# See more keys and their definitions at https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html

[dependencies]
clap = { version = "4.5.38", features = ["derive"] }

rayon = "1.10.0"
walkdir = "2.3.3"
num_cpus = "1.16.0"

[profile.release]
lto = 'fat'
codegen-units = 1
opt-level = 3
panic = 'abort'
incremental = true

Makefile.text:
CC = clang
ASFLAGS = -arch arm64 -mcpu=apple-m3 -O3 -g
SOURCES = src/main.S src/cli.S src/count.S

.PHONY: all test bench clean
all: bin/ripwc

bin/ripwc: $(SOURCES)
	mkdir -p bin
	$(CC) $(ASFLAGS) $(SOURCES) -o $@

test: bin/ripwc
	python3 tests/parity.py

bench: bin/ripwc
	python3 bench.py

clean:
	rm -f bin/ripwc

methodology: End-to-end subprocess wall-clock time, including startup, path traversal, output capture and shutdown.
Deterministic on-disk files; parity preflight before timing every selected workload.
Warm filesystem cache after preflight and warmups; no cache flushing or cold-disk claim.
Same inherited CPU availability for both processes; no affinity restriction.
One-file cases have one scanner in both implementations; upstream Rust still creates its global thread pool.
Balanced alternating execution order with a seeded randomized starting implementation per case.
Metadata-only byte counts are reported separately from scanning throughput.
Compare these executable implementations/builds on this machine, not language performance in general.
Run sequentially without concurrent tests/builds or other benchmark processes.
